solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Run on the cards for Brighton supporter? (4,5)

blocks.note: a deck is a pack of cards
to chair a meeting is to run it; 'on' puts it after DECK

annotation.surface: A gambler's streak of luck is backed by a football fan from Brighton.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brighton supporter' looks like a fan of the football club; it is the folding chair that holds you up on Brighton's seafront, a classic English beach resort.
annotation.definitionFit: A deckchair literally supports people sitting on Brighton beach.

clue.text: Passage encapsulating a historical piece (5)

indicators.note: the passage wraps round the A like a capsule

blocks.note: a duct is a passage for air or fluid
the A goes inside DUCT

annotation.surface: A corridor that holds an old museum exhibit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piece' here is a coin, as in a piece of eight; the ducat was an old European gold coin.
annotation.definitionFit: A ducat is a gold coin from past centuries, so a historical piece of money.

clue.text: Challenger in blue and red? (9)

blocks.note: blue is the colour of the Conservatives, CON for short
red, inflamed skin is tender

annotation.surface: A boxer entering the ring in blue and red colours.
annotation.walkthrough: Blue and red look like a pair of kit colours, but blue is the Conservative Party (the UK's Tories) and red is a sore patch of skin. The question mark flags that loose link.
annotation.definitionFit: A contender is someone who challenges for a title.

clue.text: Individual account breaks set of rules (9)

indicators.note: the account breaks into the set of rules, splitting it

blocks.note: a charter sets out rules or rights
AC = account, as in a/c

annotation.surface: One person's story disrupts a rulebook.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Individual' reads like an adjective describing the account; it is a noun, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A character is a person, especially a distinctive one: an individual.

clue.text: After one musical, prepare to shoot another one (5,3,4,3)

blocks.note: Annie, the show about Little Orphan Annie, is the first musical
an instruction to arm yourself before shooting

annotation.surface: A theatre-goer, fresh from one show, readies a camera to film the next.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' suggests filming a second musical; it means firing a gun. The definition 'another one' leans on 'musical' earlier in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Annie Get Your Gun is the Irving Berlin musical about Annie Oakley, a second musical after Annie.

clue.text: House in quarter of an acre collapsed: that was painful for spirit (5,10)

indicators.note: the house goes inside the quarter-acre

blocks.note: a rood is an old measure of land, a quarter of an acre
house is another name for bingo, and the call on a full card
fell = collapsed
what you say when something hurts

annotation.surface: A house on a small plot fell down, a painful blow for morale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'House' is the game bingo, not a building, and 'spirit' is a sprite rather than morale. Robin Goodfellow is another name for Puck, the mischievous fairy of English folklore.
annotation.definitionFit: Robin Goodfellow is a household sprite of English folklore, a spirit.

clue.text: Dead formidable (5)

blocks.note: slang for a corpse, rigid after death
as in hard to beat, of a test or opposition

annotation.walkthrough: Two words that read as one phrase, 'dead formidable' meaning very formidable, but each separately means STIFF.
annotation.definitionFit: Stiff means dead in slang and difficult or formidable in 'stiff opposition'.

clue.text: As spacious in certain houses (5)

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer inside it, as a house holds its occupants

blocks.note: the last letter of spacious, the whole of 'in', and the first two of certain

annotation.surface: An estate agent's line about roomy properties.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Houses' looks like the buildings the agent is selling; it is a verb meaning contains.
annotation.definitionFit: 'As' and 'since' both mean because: as it rained, since it rained.

clue.text: Japanese pots: I ruin one (5)

blocks.note: used as is
to mar is to spoil or ruin
I = one, the Roman numeral

annotation.surface: A clumsy confession from someone who has just broken a piece of oriental pottery.
annotation.walkthrough: The colon makes the clue read as a guilty admission, which neatly fits the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Imari is Japanese porcelain named after the port it was shipped from.

clue.text: Jack perhaps set about burying old bean (9)

indicators.note: 'about' as in 'about turn', so the set faces the other way and reads backwards
the turned set closes over the O, which is buried in it

blocks.note: a jack is a ship's flag, as in Union Jack
a tele is a television set; turned about it becomes ELET
O = old, as in OE for Old English

annotation.surface: A man named Jack plants an ancient bean in the ground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jack' reads as a man's name, and 'Jack' of beanstalk fame makes a bean feel natural, but here it is the flag.
annotation.definitionFit: A flageolet is a small pale French kidney bean.

clue.text: Captive, one dined upon by brown bear (7)

indicators.note: eaten by the brown, so the one ends up inside it

blocks.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
tan is a light brown
I = one, the Roman numeral; it goes inside TAN

annotation.surface: A prisoner is eaten by a brown bear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brown bear' reads as one animal; the two words split, and 'bear' is a verb, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To contain something is to hold or bear it, as a vessel bears its load.

clue.text: Neckerchief, item that’s curved round forehead, finally (7)

indicators.note: the fruit goes round the letter
takes the last letter of forehead

blocks.note: a banana is famously curved
the last letter of foreheaD

annotation.surface: A scarf described as something that curves round the brow.
annotation.walkthrough: A bandana worn round the forehead fits the surface, but the curved item is a piece of fruit.
annotation.definitionFit: A bandana is a patterned square of cloth worn at the neck or on the head.

clue.text: Eighth of twenty-four retired volunteers (5)

blocks.note: the definite article, which goes with the old name of a force that has been retired
TA = Territorial Army, Britain's reserve of volunteer soldiers

annotation.surface: A fraction of a group of volunteers who have stood down.
annotation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was renamed the Army Reserve in 2014, so 'the TA' is a retired name. 'Twenty-four' is the number of letters in the Greek alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the 24-letter Greek alphabet.

clue.text: See wire in explosive, famously the shorter one of two? (5,4)

definitions.text: famously the shorter one of two?

indicators.note: the letters are blown apart and land in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Instructions for a bomb: look for the wire inside the charge, the shorter of two.
annotation.walkthrough: Ernie Wise was the shorter half of Morecambe and Wise, the much-loved British comedy double act; 'the shorter one of two' sounds like the bomb-disposal choice of which wire to cut.
annotation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was the short partner to the tall Eric Morecambe.

clue.text: Student, dude bagging degree after vacation (5)

indicators.note: the dude puts the degree in his bag, holding it inside
the word is emptied of its middle, leaving its outside letters

blocks.note: a cat is a cool guy in jazz slang
DEGREE with its middle vacated leaves D…E

annotation.surface: A student slacker picks up a degree once the holidays are over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After vacation' looks like the holiday season; it means the word is vacated, emptied.
annotation.definitionFit: A cadet is a student at a military or police training academy.

clue.text: Curvy feature of trap shooter (6,3)

blocks.note: the double curve of the upper lip; trap is slang for mouth
the bow Cupid shoots his arrows from

annotation.surface: Trap shooting: a sport of firing at clay targets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trap shooter' reads as someone at a clay-pigeon range; trap is British slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.
annotation.definitionFit: The Cupid's bow is the curve of the upper lip; Cupid's bow is also the weapon he shoots with.

clue.text: Moving gammy toenail, second to cut through it (9)

indicators.note: a gammy leg is lame or crooked, so the letters are bent out of order
the second pushes into the middle of the rearranged letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, rearranged to E…TIONAL
a mo is a moment, a second

annotation.surface: A chiropodist trims a lame patient's toenail.
annotation.walkthrough: Gammy is British slang for lame or injured. 'Moving' looks like it describes walking on a bad foot; it means touching the feelings.
annotation.definitionFit: Something moving stirs the emotions, so is emotional.

clue.text: Lover very soon supported by a sailor after capsizing (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is supported sits on top
the sailor phrase is turned upside down, which in a down clue reverses it

blocks.note: in a mo = in a moment
A + TAR, an old word for sailor; capsized to RATA

annotation.surface: A sweetheart will soon arrive, carried by a sailor whose boat overturned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capsizing' suits a sailor, and in a down clue it turns the letters upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who is loved, a lover.

clue.text: Plea when case’s beginning in midday trial (2,7)

indicators.note: takes the first letter of case
'in' means placed within, so the C sits inside the word for midday

blocks.note: noon = midday
the first letter of Case
test = trial

annotation.surface: A defendant's plea at a lunchtime court hearing.
annotation.walkthrough: The courtroom words 'case' and 'trial' dress up plain wordplay: a letter and a synonym for test.
annotation.definitionFit: No contest is a plea in which the accused accepts conviction without admitting guilt.

clue.text: Mediocre business reportedly shown (9)

indicators.note: as it is reported, spoken aloud

blocks.note: poor = mediocre, trade = business

annotation.surface: A news item describing a lacklustre company.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Poor trade' spoken quickly in a British accent, which drops the R, lands on PORTRAYED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a person depicted in a painting or film has been shown there.

clue.text: A Briton in cravat (5)

blocks.note: used as is
a person from Scotland, one of the peoples of Britain

annotation.surface: A British man wearing a neckscarf.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container instruction but only joins wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad cravat, named after the racecourse where it was worn.

clue.text: Thin dresses seem, initially, really immoral (9)

indicators.note: the thin word is wrapped around the others like clothing
takes the first letter of seem

blocks.note: to dilute is to thin
the first letter of Seem
so = really, as in so good

annotation.surface: A remark that flimsy dresses look indecent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thin dresses' reads as skimpy clothing; 'thin' is a verb and 'dresses' a container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Dissolute means lax in morals, given to vice.

clue.text: Cut topping of sauce on cornet? (5)

indicators.note: the top letter of sauce, which in a down clue is its first

blocks.note: the first letter of Sauce
a cornet is a brass horn

annotation.surface: Sauce poured over an ice-cream cone.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a cornet is also an ice-cream cone, which with sauce is where the surface goes; here it is the instrument, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Shorn means cut, as a sheep's fleece is cut off.

clue.text: Nothing good is mothballed (2,3)

blocks.note: O = nothing, zero
nice = good

annotation.surface: A grumble that nothing of value survives being put in storage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nothing good' reads as one phrase; split it into its two parts.
annotation.definitionFit: A project on ice is shelved for later, just as a mothballed one is.

clue.text: Keeper’s disappointment having dropped header (5)

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, its head

blocks.note: DOWNER, a letdown, loses its first letter D

annotation.surface: A goalkeeper's dismay after fumbling a header.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keeper' and 'header' conjure a football goal; the keeper is simply someone who keeps something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the person a pet or a shop belongs to is its keeper, as in shopkeeper.

clue.text: On top of tree, that is secure again (5)

indicators.note: the top letter of tree, its first in a down clue

blocks.note: re = on, about, as in a memo heading
the first letter of Tree
i.e. = that is

annotation.surface: Instructions to fasten something back at the top of a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On top of' reads as one phrase of position; 'On' is RE and 'top of' works only on tree.
annotation.definitionFit: The RE- prefix means again, and a knot is what secures a rope or lace.

clue.text: Hoot with gusto on a pub crawl? (7)

blocks.note: to hoot at someone is to boo them
zing = energy, gusto

annotation.surface: A rowdy night of drinking round the pubs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hoot' suggests a riotously fun time, which a pub crawl may be; it means jeer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a pub crawl, drinking at pub after pub, is one form of heavy drinking; the question mark flags that.

clue.text: Home on pasture most inadequate (7)

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word
a nest is a bird's home; 'on' puts it after LEA

annotation.surface: A farmhouse on poor grazing land.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Most inadequate' seems to describe the pasture; it is the definition, as in the leanest year.
annotation.definitionFit: Lean means meagre, so the leanest is the most inadequate.

clue.text: Grimace, get cold and freeze in the end (5)

indicators.note: takes the last letter of freeze

blocks.note: to win something is to get it
C = cold, as on a tap
the last letter of freezE

annotation.surface: A pained face from catching a chill and finally freezing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get cold' reads as one phrase; 'get' and 'cold' give separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are the involuntary twist of the face at sudden pain or embarrassment.

clue.text: City reportedly was aware of move involving King (9)

indicators.note: what is reported is heard spoken, so the word is taken by its sound
the move is one that involves the king

blocks.note: knew = was aware of
castling in chess moves the king and a rook together

annotation.surface: A city that knew about a royal manoeuvre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'King' looks like a monarch; it is the chess piece, and castling is the one move that shifts king and rook at once.
annotation.definitionFit: Newcastle upon Tyne is a city in north-east England.
